Tip-based metrics of a known trait history

Source: R/traits_history.R
tip_history_metrics.Rd

Computes, for each tip, the metrics of trait evolution of Luza et al. (2021) from a history of a discrete trait, as Herodotools::calc_tip_based_trait_evo() computes them from a stochastic character map. Applied to a history from trait_mk(), they are the true values that a reconstruction from the tips should recover. Two metrics in continuous time are added, which count the changes inside branches too.

Usage

tip_history_metrics(history)

Arguments

history

A simmap tree, from trait_mk() or phytools.

Value

Data frame with one row per tip and the columns transitions, total_nodes, prop_transitions, last_transition_time, stasis_time, changes and time_since_change.

Details

Following the code of calc_tip_based_trait_evo(), the state of a node is the state at the start of the edges that leave it, and the path of a tip runs from its parent node to the root. transitions counts the changes of state between consecutive nodes of the path, starting from the state of the tip; prop_transitions divides it by the number of nodes in the path, total_nodes. last_transition_time sums the length of the terminal edge and of the edges leading to the nodes of the path, from the tip towards the root, while their state is the state of the tip; the root, which has no edge leading to it, adds nothing. stasis_time is the longest time spent in one state within a single edge, over the terminal edge and the edges leading to the nodes of the path. Only nodes enter transitions and last_transition_time, so changes that revert within a branch are missed; changes counts every change along the path from the root to the tip and time_since_change is the time since the last of them, or the age of the tip from the root when there was none.

References

Luza, A. L., Maestri, R., Debastiani, V. J., Patterson, B. D., Hartz, S. M., & Duarte, L. D. S. (2021). Is evolution faster at ecotones? A test using rates and tempo of diet transitions in Neotropical Sigmodontinae (Rodentia, Cricetidae). Ecology and Evolution, 11, 18676–18690. doi:10.1002/ece3.8476

Examples

set.seed(1)
tr <- treeshapesim::sim_tree_shape(10)
h <- trait_mk(tr, q = 0.5, states = c("forest", "open"))
h$states
#>       t1       t2       t3       t4       t5       t6       t7       t8 
#>   "open"   "open" "forest"   "open"   "open" "forest" "forest"   "open" 
#>       t9      t10 
#>   "open"   "open" 
tip_history_metrics(h)
#>     transitions total_nodes prop_transitions last_transition_time stasis_time
#> t1            0           3             0.00            1.0000000   0.7085115
#> t2            0           4             0.00            1.0000000   0.7085115
#> t3            1           4             0.25            0.1435450   0.7085115
#> t4            0           2             0.00            1.0000000   0.7085115
#> t5            0           3             0.00            1.0000000   0.4696704
#> t6            1           4             0.25            0.3535646   0.4696704
#> t7            1           4             0.25            0.3535646   0.4696704
#> t8            0           3             0.00            1.0000000   0.4696704
#> t9            0           4             0.00            1.0000000   0.4696704
#> t10           0           4             0.00            1.0000000   0.4696704
#>     changes time_since_change
#> t1        0        1.00000000
#> t2        0        1.00000000
#> t3        1        0.02466665
#> t4        0        1.00000000
#> t5        0        1.00000000
#> t6        1        0.27902759
#> t7        1        0.27902759
#> t8        0        1.00000000
#> t9        0        1.00000000
#> t10       0        1.00000000
# rates that vary among branches
g <- trait_mk(tr, q = 0.5, alpha = 0.3)
round(g$edge_rates, 2)
#>  [1] 0.14 0.40 0.22 1.87 1.52 0.00 2.22 0.88 0.15 0.03 0.40 1.67 0.29 0.00 0.00
#> [16] 0.46 0.50 0.03
hr <- trait_mk(tr, q = 0.5, rate_classes = c(slow = 0.1, fast = 2), class_switch = 0.2)
hr$classes
#>     t1     t2     t3     t4     t5     t6     t7     t8     t9    t10 
#> "slow" "slow" "slow" "slow" "slow" "slow" "slow" "slow" "slow" "fast"
